answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making each extra identity progressively more expensive: the first identity costs a small refundable deposit, but every additional identity registered by the same operator must post double the work and fee. A public beacon publishes the current cost schedule, so a cipher identity key cannot hide how many siblings it has, and a sudden plume of new accounts is priced out before it can vote or claim rewards. Honest users pay almost nothing; an attacker trying to run thousands of fake agents faces an exponentially rising bill.
